newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: SHANGHAI, April 29 (Reuer) - Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Tuesday with early-maturing contracts losing sharply due to the approaching Labour Day holiday, traders said.

The market and stock markets will be closed from Thursday to Sunday for the Labour Day holiday, removing a few days of use from the early-maturing contracts which depressed market sentiment on Tuesday, they said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 9.00 percent from 13.91 percent on Monday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell sharply to 5.7 million lots from 12.8 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"There will be only one trading day before the holiday. Most institutions are reluctant to build positions, in particualr in the short-term contracts," said one trader.
But a number of new domestic A share issues on Tuesday and Wednesday supported the rates, preventing them from plunging, traders said.
Traders said they believed the contracts would continue to move down on Wednesday due to the holiday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai closed up on Monday with the recent redemptions of matured state debt issues making funds flow into the spot market, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 119.66 yuan from 119.10 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose to 1.2 million lots from 939,356 lots.
Traders said they expected prices to move around the current level on Wednesday.
